title: rawgentic multi-issue driver campaign state
description: Schema for a multi-issue driver campaign state file (design #134, #148, #163). The LIVE per-campaign instance is written at runtime to claude_docs/.driver-state/<campaign>.json (disk-persisted working state, gitignored); this schema + the example-*.campaign.json files are the git-tracked contract-of-record. schema_version 2 adds issues[].depends_on (v1 files, which omit it, still validate).

schema_version.description: 1 = original queue; 2 = adds dependency DAG (issues[].depends_on) + epic anchor. A v2 reader must accept v1 files.

campaign.description: Campaign identifier; matches the <campaign>.json live-state filename.

deps_satisfied_by.description: When a dependency counts as satisfied for the advance rule (v2). Default merged.

base_default_branch_sha.description: origin/<default> HEAD when the campaign started (rollback-anchor baseline).

epic.description: Epic issue number whose task list anchors the queue (v2). null for an inline queue.

notes.description: Campaign ledger — dated free-text entries (DEFER surfacing, rate-limit window resets, mid-loop status changes). The state file IS the ledger.

depends_on.description: Issue numbers this issue depends on (v2). Absent on v1 files.

deferred_reason.description: DEFER taxonomy: owner-decision | owner-reserved | cross-repo | budget | cross-issue-dependency.

branch_preservation.description: Deterministic on DEFER: pushed (resumable, ≥1 commit) | discarded (approach abandoned) | none (no commits).

campaign_wait.description: Campaign-level terminal-for-now wait (#943, epic #871 AC 5). Absent or null means not waiting. Deliberately NOT a value of issues[].status, which is a closed vocabulary enforced by record_child_outcome and validate_driver_state; this is an additive top-level field, so no schema_version bump is required. clears_when is required: a pause whose exit condition nobody can state is a stall wearing a pause's clothes.

preferred_transport.description: #927. The campaign's DURABLE transport preference, recorded once at creation from a herdr capability probe. The per-transition EFFECT is never stored here -- it lives in `transitions`, so a stale effect cannot become the next boundary's default.

session_mode.description: DEPRECATED (#927). A write-only compatibility PROJECTION derived from `preferred_transport` at the single locked writer, so a build rolled back to a pre-#927 version still behaves correctly. Never a source of truth: when both are present, `preferred_transport` wins. Removed in a later cleanup issue.

advisory_deliveries.description: #927 PR 2. Append-only advisory DELIVERY record. A `pending` event is the CLAIM to print a transition's degradation advisory -- written under the lock before the print, so two surfaces (`handoff`, `next-child`) cannot both emit it. An `emitted` or `failed` event closes the claim. This buys at-most-once PRINTING, not exactly-once delivery: a `pending` with no `emitted` means nobody saw the line, and that is deliberately the visible defect rather than a risk of duplicate output.

transition_id.description: Keyed on transition_id, NOT generation: `creation` and `boundary_resume` do not bump a generation and would collide.

transport_audit.description: #927 PR 2. Who changed `preferred_transport` by the sanctioned `transport set` command, when, and why. Operator-supplied strings are bounded and control-character-free before they land here.

boundary_sweeps.description: #769. Append-only record of the child-boundary LEARNINGS sweep -- the owner's D181 standing order mechanized. Revalidation asks whether the remaining issue bodies still describe reality at this head; the sweep asks the wider question of whether they still make sense given what the completed child LEARNED. That judgment is not observable from state, so the validator checks COVERAGE and record integrity ONLY, never the quality of the reasoning. Replay identity is (swept_at_head, after_issue), not the head alone: a deferred or abandoned child moves no commit, so two genuine boundaries can share one head. A differing record at one identity is refused at the writer, so state stays single-valued and there is no durable conflict state to repair.

swept_at_head.description: The 40-char origin/<default> sha the sweep was performed against, re-compared under the state lock before the write so an assessment cannot be stamped with a head that moved under it.

after_issue.description: The disposed child whose learnings drove this sweep, or null when origin/main moved with no child completing (an unplanned blocker fix between children). Validated as a disposed child of this queue; never absent.

learnings.description: What the boundary taught. Required and non-empty: a record of what was swept but not what it was swept AGAINST is far less use to a successor.

assessments.description: Exactly one entry per remaining eligible child (status not merged/deferred/abandoned) -- set EQUALITY, so both a missing child and a foreign one are refused.

outcome.description: A closed vocabulary. `blocked` was in the design draft and was deleted: nothing consumed it, so a child recorded as needing a decision would still have been handed out. Blocking belongs to pending_disposition and the #944 owner gate.

note.description: Required even for `unaffected`. The negative result is the common case and must be cheap but not free -- 'does not touch the transport probe' is a complete, truthful note.

ref.description: Required when the outcome is `commented` or `rescoped`, and grammar-checked as an https:// URL or a repository-relative docs/ or claude_docs/ path. A claim that a child CHANGED must point at the artifact; checking only length would let 'done' satisfy it.

body_hash.description: The normalized hash of the body actually assessed. RECORDED, not compared: boundary_sweep_status does not diff it against the live issue, because that would make a pure state function do network I/O. The same limitation exists in the revalidation receipt this mirrors.

transitions.description: #927. Append-only two-event log. A `resolution` lands BEFORE any action; a `terminal_outcome` closes it afterwards, correlated by `resolution_id`. A resolution with no terminal event is the crash signature reconciliation keys on -- so events are appended, never rewritten.

outcome.description: Present ONLY on a terminal event.

split_attempted.description: Set BEFORE the split is called. With successor_pane null it means INDETERMINATE, never 'nothing was created'.

panes_before.description: Inventory baseline so a reclaim can diff instead of trusting a null.
